headline: Record profit on loan growth, lower expenses
summary_short: M&T Bank's Q2 2026 net income rose to $818M, up 23.2% q/q and 14.2% y/y, on record diluted EPS of $5.32 (+28.8% q/q), as $3.0B of average loan growth and a 6% q/q drop in noninterest expense lifted returns.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 2.3% q/q and 4.6% y/y to $1,792M on an extra calendar day, higher interest income from nonaccrual loans, and $3.0B of average loan growth (incl. $2.3B commercial & industrial); NIM held at 3.70%. Noninterest income grew 7.4% q/q to $740M on higher trust income, swap-related trading gains, and a $47M Bayview Lending Group distribution. Noninterest expense fell 6% q/q to $1,349M on seasonally lower salaries/benefits after 1Q's stock-comp and payroll-tax step-up. Provision for credit losses eased to $120M as nonaccrual loans fell to $1.2B. M&T repurchased $465M of stock; CET1 is estimated at 10.19%. No numeric forward guidance was given in this release.

drivers.explanation: Rose q/q on an additional calendar day, higher interest income on nonaccrual loans, and growth in average earning assets; NIM held at 3.70%. Y/y growth reflects loan and securities growth plus favorable repricing.

Growth reflects higher trust income from institutional services and wealth management (incl. seasonal tax fees), higher interest-rate-swap trading gains, and a $47M Bayview Lending Group distribution.
Rise reflects combined effects of NII growth (+2.3% q/q), noninterest income growth (+7.4% q/q), a 6% q/q decline in noninterest expense, and lower provision for credit losses ($120M vs $140M q/q).
Y/y decline reflects interest-bearing deposits at banks being deployed into loan originations and investment-securities purchases, per the release's average-balance discussion.
CFO Daryl Bible attributed record per-share earnings to strong contributions from commercial, retail, institutional services and wealth-management businesses across the franchise.
